## 🎯 Content and goals

- You can estimate and interpret a simple regression, including its uncertainty.
- You understand the logic behind multiple linear regression and how to interpret it.
- You understand the logic behind different models for interaction effects.
- You can choose the right functional form based on the visual analysis of the data.
- You know the steps of a regression analysis.

The whole lecture follows one question through one data set: *What determines
the weekly earnings of market research analysts — and do women earn less?* The
data are 252 market research analysts from the US Current Population Survey
2014 [@bekes2021data]. The
[lab session on Friday](/content/material/s_10_LinearModels.qmd) rebuilds every
model of the lecture in R, on exactly the same data.

::: {.callout-important}
## Prerequisite: the statistics recap
The lecture builds directly on the track
[A Recap of Undergraduate Statistics](https://euf-methodology-hub.netlify.app/tracks/statistics-recap)
on *Method and Inquiry*. In particular, it assumes that you know the regression
line as a descriptive tool, residuals, sampling distributions, standard errors,
hypothesis tests and confidence intervals. These concepts are not repeated in
the lecture.
:::

## 📚 Mandatory Reading

- @ismay2025moderndive [chapters 5--6] — the lecture uses its terminology
  (*parallel slopes model* vs *interaction model*)

## 🏆 Further Readings

- @jamesIntroductionStatisticalLearning2021 [chapter 3]
- On *Method and Inquiry*, as companions to the lecture:
  - [Categorical Variables and Interaction Terms in Regression](https://euf-methodology-hub.netlify.app/resources/multiple-regression-categorical-interactions)
    [@graebner2026-multiple-regression-categorical-interactions] — same data
    set as the lecture
  - [Regression Residuals and Model Diagnostics](https://euf-methodology-hub.netlify.app/resources/regression-residuals-diagnostics)
    [@graebner2026-regression-residuals-diagnostics]
  - [Causal Reasoning with DAGs](https://euf-methodology-hub.netlify.app/resources/reasoning-with-dags)
    [@graebner2026-reasoning-with-dags] — on which variables to control for
- On the role of working hours in the gender pay gap: @goldin2014grand; for an
  overview of the literature: @blau2017gender

## ✍️ Exercises and coursework

- Work through the
  [lab session 10](/content/material/s_10_LinearModels.qmd), which implements
  the lecture in R, and complete its coursework: a short Quarto report that
  applies the six steps of a regression analysis to a new data set.
- Answer the recap questions at the end of the slides.
